summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease and a history of a failed kidney transplant was admitted for high fever and chills. Blood cultures grew E. coli, indicating bacteremia. Despite an extensive prior workup for fever of unknown origin, imaging and functional testing revealed acute cholecystitis as the likely source. She underwent an open cholecystectomy, after which her fever resolved. She completed a course of intravenous antibiotics, transitioned to oral cefpodoxime, and recovered well. Her warfarin was adjusted postoperatively, and she was treated for oral and vaginal candidiasis. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue dialysis, medications, and monitor for signs of infection.
problems: Septicemia due to escherichia coli [E. coli]
Calculus of gallbladder with acute cholecystitis, without mention of obstruction
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of other parts of uterus
Acquired absence of both cervix and uterus
